text: WHAT ABOUT WUCHANG?

label: text
text: Poking, August 23.

label: text
text: Nanking telegrams quote General Sun Chuan-fang as stating that the position in Hupeh is obviously critical and, if the Southerners occupied Wuchang and Hankow, it would be worse. Consequently he has ordered part of his force to prepare for mobilisation. He is closely watching the situation, and his force might participate against the southerners.

label: text
text: Siberian passengers arriving at Harbjn on Friday assert that General Feng Yushiang, in a special ear, accompanied them as far as Verknedinsk, where he remained on August 24. According to other information Feng subsequently went on to Urga.-Reuter.

label: text
text: Shanghai, August 28.

label: text
text: Some sensation was created yesterday when, apparently under orders from Sun Chuan-fang, all the Chinese of the so-called Volunteers of Chapel and Nantao districts of Shanghai, numbering seven hundred, were disarmed.

label: text
text: They were ordered to a parade without arms yesterday morning when they were informed that their corps was dissolved. Some were despatched to Nailing possibly for enrolment in the Army. Reuter.

label: paragraph_title
text: TANGIER QUESTION TO BE DEFERRED.

label: text
text: LEAGUE COUNCIL FIRST

label: text
text: London, Aug. 28.

label: text
text: It is confirmed in well-informed sources in London that Spain has suggested a conference at Geneva on Wednesday to consider the Spanish claim to Tangier on the eve of the League Council meeting.

label: text
text: It is understood that Great Britain will reply at the earliest. There is a natural reluctance at present to discuss the terms of the reply, but the general impression is that no useful purpose will be served by a conference at short notice which should be postponed till after the League Council meeting, the primary object of which is to arrange for Germany's admission to the League and no extraneous issues should be permitted to interfere.

label: text
text: It is expected that France will support Great Britain.—Reuter. Italian Support.

label: text
text: Italy has replied to the Spanish Note, assuring her of Italy's desire to meet all Spain's just demands, and agreeing to Spain's suggestion that "the Tangier problem should be submitted to an International Conference of the Powers interested. Italian political circles infer from this that the Italian Government is unwilling that the problem should be submitted to the League of Nation's Reuter.

U.S. NAVAL RATINGS
LANDED.

label: text
text:
Washington, August 28.
The United States cruiser, Galveston, landed two hundred ratings at Bluefields, Nicaragua, to protect foreign life and property, in response to an appeal from the Governor that the local forces would be unable to guarantee protection. Reuter's American Service.

label: text
text:
Mexico City, August 28:
The allegations contained in the Nicaragua Note to the League of Nations, are denied by the Foreign Minister and the Minister for Nicaragua. The former points out that the League has nothing to do with Mexico.—Reuter's American Service.

label: paragraph_title

label: text
text: SHANGHAI SCENES.

label: text
text: Shanghai, August 28.

label: text
text: Student demonstrations took place locally in connection with the "Red Strike propaganda." Students gathered in Nanking Road, waving flags and making demonstrations against the Japanese mill owners.

label: text
text: The Police were fully prepared and dispersed the demonstrators, but at one time it was necessary to make a baton charge.

label: text
text: "In the northern district the position looked serious, but the Police succeeded in controlling attempts at rioting, the agitators retreating to the Chinese territory."

label: text
text: Several students have been arrested for distributing Red pamphlets.

label: text
text: The demonstrations emphasise the seriousness of the labour situation in Shanghai. Reuter.

label: text
text: Against the Japanese.

label: text
text: Judging by the handbills distributed during the disturbances yesterday, as the result of the agitation after the death of a Chinese howker, about a Japanese ship, they were directed only against the Japanese.

label: text
text: Eighteen of the agitations have been arrested, and the total arrests during the weekend number thirty-four. The mill situation in Shanghai is unchanged, but it is better at Footung.—Renter.

text: Commander John Rodgers, survivor of the seaplane which was lost en route to Hawaii on September 11 last, was flying in the vicinity of the Naval Aircraft Factory when the machine nose-dived into the river, and the Commander was fatally injured. Reuter.

label: paragraph_title
text: “TIGER'S” LETTER.

label: paragraph_title
text: "RIGHT THING AT RIGHT TIME"

label: text
text: QUITE SATISFIED.

label: text
text: Vendee home on returning from shopping told some journalists that he was quite satisfied regarding his letter to President Coolidge. He thought that he had done the right thing at the right time.

label: text
text: He said that he had received numerous epistles from all over the world, but none from members of Parliamenter. There was an enormous quantity from America, especially from the American Legion, but no abuse.

label: text
text: M. Clemenceau explained that he intervened after the receipt of a most moving anonymous letter, which worried him, asking whether he was prepared to carry to his grave the responsibility for what was about to happen.

label: text
text: M. Clemencena add that he left the Coolidge letter on the table for 24 hours and then handed it to Havas Agency. He did not think that the debt settlement could be satisfied, and he had still got something left to say.

label: text
text: M. Clemenceau concluded the interview by complaining of the cost of living. Someone in the market had just offered him a lobster for 75 francs, he said adding: "73 francs for a lobster. I did not buy it," I took "carrots" instead.
